10.h: 6 - Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl al-ʿAdawī * (ع)
10.t:
Ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib, Abū al-Aʿwar, al-Qurashī, al-ʿAdawī.
One of the Ten Promised Paradise (العشرة المبشرة), one of the first forerunners among the Badrīs (البدري), and one of those with whom Allah is pleased and who are pleased with Him (2) .
He took part in the battles with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and was present at the siege of Damascus and its conquest, and he was appointed ⟦1:124⟧ over it by Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, so he was the first of this community to serve as deputy governor of Damascus (1) .
He has a few hadiths: he has two hadiths in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين)) , and al-Bukhārī alone has one further hadith from him (2) .
Narrating from him: ابن عمر، وأبو الطفيل، وعمرو بن حريث، وزر بن حبيش، وأبو عثمان النهدي، وعروة بن الزبير، وعبد الله بن ظالم، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، وطائفة.
قرأت على أحمد بن عبد الحميد، أخبركم الإمام أبو محمد بن قدامة سنة ثمان عشرة وست مائة، أخبرتنا شهدة بنت أحمد الكاتبة بقراءتي، أنبأنا طراد بن محمد الزينبي، أنبأنا ابن رزقويه، أنبأنا أبو جعفر محمد بن يحيى الطائي سنة تسع وثلاثين وثلاث مائة، حدثنا علي بن حرب، حدثنا سفيان، عن عبد الملك بن عمير، عن عمرو بن حريث، عن سعيد بن زيد بن عمرو:
From the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (Truffles are of the manna that Allah sent down upon the Children of Israel, and their water is a cure for the eye) .
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3) by way of Ibn ʿUyaynah, so it has reached us as a substitute route (البدل) with an elevated chain (العالي). ⟦1:125⟧
قرأت على علي بن عيسى التغلبي، أخبركم محمد بن إبراهيم الصوفي سنة عشرين وست مائة، أنبأنا أبو طاهر السلفي، أنبأنا عبد الله الثقفي، أنبأنا أحمد بن الحسن، أنبأنا حاجب بن أحمد، حدثنا عبد الرحيم، هو ابن منيب، حدثنا سفيان، عن الزهري، عن طلحة:
From Saʿīd ibn Zayd, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (Whoever wrongfully takes a span of land, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths; and whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr (1)) .
This is a hadith with an acceptable chain of transmission (الإسناد), but there is a break in it, because Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwf did not hear it from Saʿīd.
Mālik, Yūnus and a group narrated it from al-Zuhrī, and they inserted between Ṭalḥah and Saʿīd: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl (2) al-Anṣārī.
Recorded by al-Bukhārī, from Abū al-Yamān, from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī.
His father Zayd (3) ibn ʿAmr was one of those who fled to Allah from the worship of idols; he travelled through the land of Syria seeking the upright religion, and he saw the Christians and the Jews and disliked their religion, ⟦1:126⟧ and said: O Allah, I am upon the religion of Abraham (1) ; but he did not attain the law of Abraham (peace be upon him) as it ought to be, nor did he see anyone who could acquaint him with it. He is among the people of salvation, for the Prophet ﷺ bore witness for him that: (He will be raised as a nation by himself (2)) .
He was the paternal cousin of the Imam (الإمام) ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; he saw the Prophet ﷺ, but did not live until he was sent.
Yūnus ibn Bukayr, who was one of the vessels of knowledge of the biographies, transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said:
There was a group of Quraysh: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Waraqah ibn Nawfal, ʿUthmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Asad, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, and Umaymah daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; they were present with Quraysh at an idol of theirs, at which they used to sacrifice for one of their festivals. When they had gathered, those few drew aside with one another and said: Be true to one another, and keep one another's secret.
Then one of them said: You know -by Allah- that your people are upon nothing; they have missed the religion of Abraham and contravened it. What is an idol that is worshipped, which neither harms nor benefits? So seek for yourselves.
He said: So they went out searching and travelling through the land, seeking people of scripture among the Jews, the Christians and all the religions, in quest of the Ḥanīfiyyah.
As for Waraqah: he became a Christian and became firmly established in Christianity, acquired the books, and learned a great deal of knowledge.
None of them was of more upright conduct than Zayd: he shunned the idols and the religions, except the religion of Abraham; he affirmed the oneness of Allah the Exalted, and did not eat of the sacrifices of his people.
Al-Khaṭṭāb, his paternal uncle, had harmed him, so he moved away from him to the upper part of Mecca and stayed at Ḥirāʾ; al-Khaṭṭāb set some foolish youths over him who would not let him enter Mecca, so he would enter it only secretly. Al-Khaṭṭāb was also his brother through his mother, and he used to blame him for abandoning his religion. So Zayd travelled to Syria, al-Jazīrah and Mosul, asking about religion (3) . ⟦1:127⟧
أخبرنا يوسف بن أحمد بن أبي بكر الحجار، أنبأنا موسى بن عبد القادر، أنبأنا سعيد بن أحمد بن (1) البنا (ح) .
وأنبأنا أحمد بن المؤيد، أنبأنا الحسن بن إسحاق، أخبرنا محمد بن عبيد الله بن الزاغوني، وقرأت على عمر بن عبد المنعم في سنة ثلاث وتسعين، عن أبي اليمن الكندي إجازة في سنة ثمان وست مائة، أنبأنا أبو الفضل محمد بن عبد الله بن المهتدي بالله قالوا:
أنبأنا محمد بن محمد الزينبي، أنبأنا محمد بن عمر الوراق، حدثنا عبد الله بن سليمان، حدثنا عيسى بن حماد، أنبأنا الليث بن سعد، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر، قالت:
I saw Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl standing, leaning his back against the Kaʿbah, saying: O people of Quraysh! By Allah, none of you is upon the religion of Abraham except me.
And he used to save the girl who was to be buried alive: he would say to a man when he wanted to kill his daughter: Stop, do not kill her; I will spare you her upkeep. So he would take her, and when she had grown up he would say to her father: If you wish, I will hand her over to you, and if you wish, I will spare you her upkeep (2) .
This is an authentic (الصحيح), gharīb (الغريب) hadith; al-Layth alone narrated it, and he narrates it from Hishām only in writing.
Al-Bukhārī cited it without a chain in (his Ṣaḥīḥ (3)) , saying: al-Layth said: Hishām wrote to me, and he mentioned it.
Ibn Isḥāq heard it from Hishām, ⟦1:128⟧ and I have, by the aforementioned chain of transmission (الإسناد) to al-Layth from Hishām (1) , a manuscript copy; among the most objectionable things in it is: from his father ʿUrwah, that he said:
Waraqah ibn Nawfal passed by Bilāl while he was being tortured, his back pressed against the scorching ground, and he was saying: One, One.
Waraqah said: One, One, O Bilāl; patience, O Bilāl. Why do you torture him? By Him in Whose hand is my soul, if you kill him, I will take him as an object of tenderness.
He means: I will surely touch him for blessing.
This is mursal (مرسل); had Waraqah lived to see this, he would have been counted among the Companions (الصحابي); but the man died during the lull in revelation, after the prophethood and before the messengership, as is in the Ṣaḥīḥ (2) .
يونس بن بكير: عن ابن إسحاق، حدثني هشام، عن أبيه، عن أسماء:
That Waraqah used to say: O Allah, if I knew the way most beloved to You, I would worship You by it, but I do not know; then he would prostrate on his palm (3) .
يونس بن بكير وعدة: عن المسعودي، عن نفيل بن هشام بن سعيد بن زيد، عن أبيه، عن جده قال:
Zayd ibn ʿAmr passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, and they invited him to a meal-spread of theirs, and he said:
O son of my brother! I do not eat of what has been sacrificed on the stone altars. And after that day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never seen eating of what had been sacrificed on the stone altars.
Al-Masʿūdī: not an authority (الحجة).
Recorded by the Imam (الإمام) Aḥmad in (his Musnad) , from Yazīd, from al-Masʿūdī; then he added at its end: Saʿīd (4) said:
I said: O Messenger of Allah! My father was as you saw and as has reached you; had he lived to see you, he would have believed in you and followed you, so ask forgiveness for him.
He said: (Yes, I will ask forgiveness for him, for he ⟦1:129⟧ will be raised as a nation by himself (1)) .
Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī narrated it, saying:
حدثنا إبراهيم بن محمد، حدثنا أبو قطن، عن المسعودي، عن نفيل، عن أبيه، عن جده قال:
Zayd passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ibn Ḥārithah while they were eating from a meal-spread, and they invited him.
He said: I do not eat of what has been sacrificed on the stone altars.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never seen eating of what had been sacrificed on the stone altars (2) .
This wording is fine; it explains what preceded it. The Chosen One was ever guarded and protected, before the revelation and after it. And even if the permissibility of that were conceivable, we know by necessity that he used to eat of the sacrifices of ⟦1:130⟧ Quraysh before the revelation, and that was under permissibility; their sacrifices were described as forbidden only after the revelation of the verse, just as wine was permitted until its prohibition was revealed in Medina after the day of Uḥud.
What admits no doubt is that he was protected, before the revelation and after it, and before the law was laid down, from fornication definitively, and from treachery, perfidy, lying, drunkenness, prostrating to an idol, and seeking divination with arrows, and from base acts, foolishness, foul speech and exposing his nakedness; he did not circumambulate naked, nor did he stand on the day of ʿArafah with his people at Muzdalifah; rather he would stand at ʿArafah.
In any case, had anything of that appeared from him, there would have been no blame on him, because he did not know; but the rank of perfection refuses that such should occur from him - ﷺ -.
أبو معاوية: عن هشام، عن أبيه، عن عائشة:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (I entered Paradise and saw two great trees belonging to Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl) .
Gharīb (الغريب).
It was narrated by al-Bāghandī (1) , from al-Ashajj, from him.
عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن أسماء قالت:
I saw Zayd ibn ʿAmr as a very old man, leaning his back against the Kaʿbah, and he was saying: ⟦1:131⟧
Woe to you, O people of Quraysh! Beware of fornication, for it brings on poverty (1) .
أبو الحسن المدائني: عن إسماعيل بن مجالد، عن أبيه، عن الشعبي، عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن الخطاب قال:
Zayd ibn ʿAmr said: I sampled Christianity and Judaism and disliked them both. I was in Syria, and I came to a monk and related my affair to him.
He said: I see that you want the religion of Abraham (peace be upon him), O brother of the people (2) of Mecca; you are seeking a religion that is not to be found today. So return to your land, for Allah will send from your people one who will bring the religion of Abraham, the Ḥanīfiyyah, and he is the noblest of creation in the sight of Allah (3) .
With a weak (ضعيف) chain of transmission (الإسناد), from Ḥujayr ibn Abī Ihāb, who said:
I saw Zayd ibn ʿAmr watching the sun; when it passed the meridian, he faced the Kaʿbah, prayed one rakʿah and made two prostrations.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn ʿUthmān al-Ḥizāmī recited for Zayd:
I have submitted my face to Him to Whom submit ... the rain-clouds that carry sweet, pure water
When they are made to water a land among lands ... they are driven to it and pour down in torrents (4)
And I have submitted myself to Him to Whom submits ... the earth that carries heavy rocks ⟦1:132⟧
He spread it out, and when it was level He made it firm ... evenly, and anchored the mountains upon it (1)
Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated, according to what Ibn Abī al-Zinād transmitted from him:
That it reached him that Zayd ibn ʿAmr was in Syria, and when news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached him, he set out seeking him, but the people of Mayfaʿah in Syria killed him (2) .
Al-Wāqidī narrated that he died and was buried at the foot of Ḥirāʾ; and Ibn Isḥāq said: he was killed in the land of Lakhm.
عبد العزيز (3) بن المختار: أنبأنا موسى بن عقبة، أخبرني سالم: he heard Ibn ʿUmar narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he met Zayd ibn ʿAmr at the lower part of Baldaḥ before the revelation, and a meal-spread with meat in it was presented to Zayd, but he refused to eat and said: I do not eat of what you sacrifice on your stone altars; I eat only that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned.
Recorded by al-Bukhārī, who added at its end: And he used to reproach Quraysh, saying: The sheep: Allah created it, sent down for it from the sky, and made things grow for it from the earth, then you slaughter it in other than the name of Allah (4) ?
Abū Usāmah and another both said:
حدثنا محمد بن عمرو، عن أبي سلمة، ويحيى بن ⟦1:133⟧ عبد الرحمن، عن أسامة بن زيد، عن زيد بن حارثة، قال:
I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with me riding behind him, to one of the stone altars, and we slaughtered for him - the pronoun (him) refers to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ - a sheep and placed it in the oven; when it was cooked, we put it in our meal-spread. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came along riding, with me behind him, in the days of the heat, until, when we were at the top of the valley, he met Zayd ibn ʿAmr, and each of them greeted the other.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: (Why do I see that your people have come to detest you?) That is: they hate you.
He said: By Allah, that is not from any hostility on my part toward them, but I see them in misguidance; so I went out seeking the religion until I came to the rabbis of Aylah, and I found them worshipping Allah and associating partners with Him. Then I was directed to an old man in al-Jazīrah, so I came to him and told him.
He said: Everyone you have seen is in misguidance; you are asking about a religion that is the religion of Allah and His angels, and a prophet has come forth in your land, or is about to come forth; go back to him and follow him. So I returned, but I perceived nothing.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the camel kneel, then we offered him the meal-spread.
He said: What is this?
We said: A sheep that we slaughtered for the stone altar; thus he said.
He said: I do not eat of what has been slaughtered for other than Allah. Then they parted, and Zayd died before the Mission.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (He will come as a nation by himself (1)) .
Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī narrated it in (al-Gharīb) , from two shaykhs of his, from Abū Usāmah.
Then he said: Concerning slaughtering it at the stone altar there are two possibilities:
Either Zayd did it without the command of the Prophet ﷺ, except that he was with him, so it was attributed to him, because Zayd did not have of protection and divine success ⟦1:134⟧ what Allah gave His Prophet. And how could that be permissible, when he (peace be upon him) had forbidden Zayd to touch an idol, and he himself never touched it before his prophethood? So how would he be content that a sacrifice be made to the idol? This is impossible.
The second: that he slaughtered for Allah, and it happened to be at an idol at which they used to sacrifice.
I say: This is good, for actions are only by intention.
As for Zayd, he went by the outward appearance, while the inward reality was for Allah; and perhaps the Prophet ﷺ refrained from speaking out for fear of harm, for, although we know of his aversion to idols, we also know that before the prophethood he did not openly condemn them among Quraysh, nor publicly declare his loathing of them before the Mission.
What is apparent is that Zayd (may Allah have mercy on him) died before the Mission, for Ibn Isḥāq (1) transmitted that Waraqah ibn Nawfal elegised him in verses, which are:
You were rightly guided and did well, Ibn ʿAmr, and you only ... avoided an oven of fire, blazing hot
By your religion, a Lord like Whom there is no lord, ... and your leaving the idols of the tyrants just as they are (2)
And your attaining the religion that you had sought ... and you were not heedless of the oneness of your Lord
So you have come to be in an abode whose station is noble ... being entertained therein with honour, at ease (3)
The mercy of his Lord may reach a man ... even if he were seventy valleys beneath the earth
Yes, and ʿUrwah counted Saʿīd ibn Zayd among the Badrīs (البدري), saying:
He came from Syria after Badr and spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who allotted him his share and his reward (4) .
Likewise said Mūsā ibn ⟦1:135⟧ ʿUqbah and Ibn Isḥāq.
His wife: she was his paternal cousin Fāṭimah, the sister of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
Saʿīd became Muslim before the Prophet ﷺ entered the house of al-Arqam (1) .
Al-Bukhārī recorded by three routes, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said:
Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: I have seen myself when ʿUmar was binding me because of Islam, along with his sister; and if anyone were to collapse because of what you did to ʿUthmān, it would be fitting (2) .
We have mentioned, in the account of ʿUmar's conversion to Islam, a section on this matter.
Ibn Saʿd mentioned in (his Ṭabaqāt) , from al-Wāqidī, from his men, that they said:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was awaiting the arrival of the caravan of Quraysh from Syria, he sent Ṭalḥah and Saʿīd ibn Zayd, ten days before his departure from Medina, to seek out news of the caravan. They reached al-Ḥawrāʾ and remained there until the caravan passed them, and it took to the coast.
News reached the Prophet of Allah before ⟦1:136⟧ their arrival, so he called his Companions to action and went out seeking the caravan, but it had taken to the coast, and they travelled night and day. Ṭalḥah and Saʿīd returned to inform him, and reached Medina on the day of the battle, so they went out heading for him.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted them their shares and their rewards.
Saʿīd was present at Uḥud, the Trench, al-Ḥudaybiyah and the battles (1) .
Several hadiths have already been given stating that he is among the people of Paradise and among the martyrs.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said: I asked my father about testifying for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar that they are in Paradise?
He said: Yes, go by the hadith of Saʿīd ibn Zayd.
Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father: that Arwā bint Uways claimed that Saʿīd ibn Zayd had taken something of her land, and she brought a dispute against him before Marwān.
Saʿīd said: Would I take anything of her land after what I heard from the Messenger of Allah:
I heard him say: (Whoever takes anything of land, it will be hung around his neck down to seven earths) .
Marwān said: I will not ask you for proof after this.
Saʿīd said: O Allah, if she is lying, then blind her sight and kill her in her land (2) .
She did not die until she went blind; and while she was walking in her land, she fell into a pit and died.
Recorded by Muslim (3) .
He narrated something similar: عبد العزيز بن أبي حازم، عن العلاء بن عبد ⟦1:137⟧ الرحمن (1) ، عن أبيه.
He narrated something similar: المغيرة بن عبد الرحمن، عن عبد الله بن عمر، عن نافع، عن ابن (2) عمر.
Ibn Abī Ḥāzim (3) said in his hadith: Arwā asked Saʿīd to pray for her, and said: I wronged you.
He said: I will not give back to Allah anything He has given me.
I say: Saʿīd was not behind the rank of the people of the Consultation in precedence and eminence; ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) left him out only so that there should remain for him no trace of personal interest in it, because he was his brother-in-law and his paternal cousin; had he named him among the people of the Consultation, the Rāfiḍah (الرافضة) would have said: he favoured (4) his cousin. And he excluded from it his own son and his kin.
So let the work (5) be for Allah in this way.
خالد الطحان: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن محارب بن دثار قال: a letter was written ⟦1:138⟧ by Muʿāwiyah to Marwān, the governor of Medina, that he should take the pledge of allegiance for his son Yazīd.
A man from the army of Syria said: What is holding you back?
He said: Until Saʿīd ibn Zayd comes and pledges allegiance, for he is the chief of the people of the town; when he pledges allegiance, the people will pledge allegiance.
He said: Shall I not go and bring him to you? ... , and he mentioned the hadith (1) .
أنبئنا وأخبرنا عن حنبل سماعا، أنبأنا ابن الحصين، أنبأنا ابن المذهب، أنبأنا القطيعي، حدثنا عبد الله، حدثني أبي، حدثنا وكيع، حدثنا سفيان، عن حصين ومنصور، عن هلال بن يساف، عن سعيد بن زيد - وقال حصين: عن ابن ظالم، عن سعيد بن زيد -:
That the Prophet ﷺ said: (Be still, Ḥirāʾ! For upon you there is none but a prophet, or a ṣiddīq, or a martyr) .
And upon it were the Prophet, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, Saʿd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Saʿīd ibn Zayd (2) .
ابن سعد: أنبأنا أبو ضمرة، عن يحيى بن سعيد، أخبرني نافع، عن ابن عمر:
That he was called for help concerning Saʿīd ibn Zayd on Friday, after the day had risen high, so Ibn ʿUmar came to him at al-ʿAqīq and left the Friday prayer (3) .
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (4) .
Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah said, from Nāfiʿ, who said:
Saʿīd ibn Zayd died, and he had been suffering from a bowel ailment; ⟦1:139⟧ Umm Saʿīd said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: Will you embalm him with musk?
He said: And what perfume is better than musk?
So she handed him musk (1) .
سليمان بن بلال: حدثنا الجعيد بن عبد الرحمن، عن عائشة بنت سعد قالت:
Saʿīd ibn Zayd died at al-ʿAqīq; Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ washed him and shrouded him, and went out with him (2) .
It was narrated (3) by more than one, from Mālik, who said:
Saʿīd ibn Zayd and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ died at al-ʿAqīq.
Al-Wāqidī said: Saʿīd ibn Zayd died in the year 51, aged some years over 70, and was buried in Medina; Saʿd and Ibn ʿUmar went down into his grave.
Likewise said Abū ʿUbayd, Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr and Shihāb.
Al-Wāqidī said: Saʿīd was a man of dark complexion, tall, and hairy.
Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī stood alone in saying: he died in Kufa.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿd al-Zuhrī said: he died in the year 52 (may Allah be pleased with him).
This is what could readily be given of the biography of the Ten; they are the best of Quraysh, the best of the foremost Emigrants, the best of the Badrīs (البدري), the best of the people of the Tree, and the masters of this community in this world and the Hereafter.
May Allah banish the Rāfiḍah (الرافضة)! How astray they are, and how strong their caprice! How did they acknowledge the merit of one of them, yet deprive the nine of their due, and fabricate against them (4) that they concealed the explicit text concerning ʿAlī that he was the caliph?
By Allah, nothing of that happened, nor that they diverted the matter from him, as they claim, and contravened their Prophet, and hastened to pledge allegiance to a man of Banū Taym who traded and earned his living, ⟦1:140⟧ not out of desire for his wealth, nor out of fear of (1) his clan and his men. Woe to you! Would anyone with a grain of reason do this?
Even if this were possible for one, it would not be possible for a group; and even if it were possible for it to occur from a group, it would be impossible, in this situation, for it to occur from thousands of the leading Emigrants and Helpers, the knights of the community and the heroes of Islam. But there is no remedy for curing Rafḍ, for it is a chronic disease; and guidance is a light that Allah casts into the heart of whom He wills, and there is no power except through Allah.
A hadith concerning them jointly, and it is extremely rejected (المنكر).
Al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in (al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr) : al-Ḥusayn ibn Isḥāq al-Tustarī narrated to us; and Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥamdān said: al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān narrated to us in (his Musnad) ; they both said:
حدثنا نصر بن علي، حدثنا عبد المؤمن بن عباد العبدي، حدثنا يزيد بن معن، حدثني عبد الله بن شرحبيل، عن رجل من قريش، عن زيد بن أبي أوفى -رضي الله عنه- قال:
I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque of Medina, and he began saying: (Where is so-and-so, where is so-and-so?) .
He kept looking for them and sending for them until they gathered.
He said: (I am going to tell you a hadith, so memorise it and retain it: Allah chose from His creation a creation whom He will admit to Paradise, and I am choosing from among you, and making brotherhood between you as Allah made brotherhood between the angels. Stand, O Abū Bakr) .
He stood, and he said: (You have a favour with me, for which Allah will reward you; were I to take an intimate friend, I would have taken you; you are to me as my shirt is to my body.
Come near, O ʿUmar) .
He came near, and he said: (You used to be very contentious against us, so I prayed to Allah to strengthen the religion through you or through Abū Jahl, and Allah did that through you; and you are with me in Paradise, the third of three) .
Then he made brotherhood between him and Abū Bakr.
Then he called ʿUthmān, and kept drawing him closer until he pressed his knee against his knee; then he looked up to the sky, glorified Allah three times, then said: (You have a standing among the people of heaven; you are among those who will come to me at the Basin with his jugular veins spurting blood.
And I will say: ⟦1:141⟧
Who did this to you?
And you will say: So-and-so) .
Then he called ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and said: (Come near, O trustee of Allah, and the one trusted in heaven; Allah will give you power over your wealth in truth; I have a supplication for you which I have deferred) .
He said: Choose for me, O Messenger of Allah!
He said: (You have charged me with a trust: may Allah make your wealth abundant) and he made brotherhood between him and ʿUthmān.
Then he called Ṭalḥah and al-Zubayr, and they came near him, and he said: (You two are my disciples, like the disciples of Jesus) and he made brotherhood between them.
Then he called Saʿd and ʿAmmār, and said: (O ʿAmmār! The transgressing party will kill you) then he made brotherhood between them.
Then he called Abū al-Dardāʾ and Salmān, and said: (O Salmān! You are one of us, the People of the House, and Allah has given you the first knowledge and the last knowledge. O Abū al-Dardāʾ! If you criticise them, they will criticise you; if you leave them, they will leave you; and if you flee from them, they will catch up with you; so lend them your honour for the day of your poverty) then he made brotherhood between them.
Then he looked at Ibn ʿUmar, and said: (Praise be to Allah, Who guides out of misguidance) .
ʿAlī said: O Messenger of Allah! My spirit has gone and my back is broken, since you left me out.
He said: (I have held you back only for myself; you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, and you are my heir) .
He said: What will I inherit from you?
He said: (The Book of Allah and the Sunnah (السنة) of His Prophet; and you will be with me in my palace in Paradise with Fāṭimah) , and he recited: “Brothers, on couches facing one another” (Qurʾān 15:47) .
Zayd (1) : he is not known except in this fabricated (الموضوع) hadith.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr ⟦1:142⟧ al-Ṭabarī narrated it, from Ḥusayn al-Dāriʿ, from ʿAbd al-Muʾmin, and he dropped from it: from a man.
Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm al-Simmarī (1) said: حدثنا عبد الرحيم بن واقد، حدثنا شعيب بن يونس، حدثنا موسى بن صهيب، عن يحيى بن زكريا، عن عبد الله بن شرحبيل، عن رجل، عن زيد (2) .
Muṭayyan narrated it in abridged form: حدثنا ثابت بن يعقوب، حدثنا ثابت بن حماد النصري، عن موسى بن صهيب، عن عبادة بن نسي، عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى (3) .
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥulwānī said: حدثنا شبابة بن سوار، حدثنا أبو عبد الله الباهلي - يقال اسمه: جعفر بن مرزوق - عن غياث بن شقير، عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط، عن سعيد بن عامر الجمحي:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day: (O Abū Bakr! Come; and O ʿUmar! Come) and he mentioned the hadith of the brotherhood, except that he differed in the names of the brothers, adding to them and omitting from them.
Shabābah alone narrated it, and it is not authentic (الصحيح).
What is preserved (المحفوظ) is that he made brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers, so that support and mutual aid would thereby be achieved for these through those.
Saʿīd ibn Zayd has forty-eight hadiths; the two of them agreed on two hadiths of his, and al-Bukhārī alone has a third. ⟦1:143⟧
